item.title: China unveils Shenzhou-24 crew for space station mission, including first foreign astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew members Tang Hongbo (C), Wu Yi (R), and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. (Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will carry out the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission, with Tang serving as commander, the China Manned Space Agency announced on Tuesday. The three astronauts are a spacecraft pilot, a flight engineer and a payload specialist, respectively. Tang has participated in the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 crewed flight missions and is about to become the first astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station three times. Wu comes from the country's third batch of astronauts and will embark on his first spaceflight mission. Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship is scheduled to be launched at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Zhang Jingbo, spokesperson of the agency, said at a press conference. ■ This undated photo shows Shenzhou-24 crew member Tang Hongbo. item.title: Xi extends congratulations on Int'l Day of Solidarity with Palestinian People
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping extended congratulations to a UN meeting held on Monday to commemorate the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People. In his message, Xi said that the Palestinian question lies at the heart of the Middle East issue, adding that the current tensions in the Middle East should not divert the international community's attention from the Palestinian issue. The key to resolving the Palestinian question is to stay on course toward the two-state solution and promote the resumption of peace talks between Palestine and Israel, Xi said. He stressed that the governance of the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza should be advanced in accordance with the principle of "Palestinians governing Palestine," and opposed any land-grabbing or rights-infringing actions targeting the Palestinian people. The international community should translate its consensus and commitments in support of Palestine into concrete actions, promote a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and protect the safety of civilians, Xi said. Xi said that justice will prevail and must not be absent. China has always firmly supported the just cause of the Palestinian people to restore their legitimate national rights, he said. China will continue to work with all countries that cherish peace and uphold justice to promote the early realization of a comprehensive, just and lasting solution of the Palestinian question, based on the rule of international law and with a view to addressing both its symptoms and root causes, Xi said. Such efforts will contribute to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and make positive contributions to world peace, stability, development and prosperity, Xi added. ■

item.title: Exhibition highlights contributions of international friends in wartime China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
A man visits an exhibition at the Museum of the Communist Party of China in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 23, 2026. The exhibition titled "Great Bridge Builders Edgar Snow and International Friends in Yan'an" was opened here on Monday. Featuring the individual stories and collective memories of 216 international friends, the exhibition traces a historical journey from wartime support to enduring friendship. (Xinhua/Jin Liangkuai) BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- An exhibition was launched in the Museum of the Communist Party of China (CPC) in Beijing on Monday highlighting the contributions of international friends, including American journalist Edgar Snow, during China's wartime years and paying tribute to friendships that transcended national borders. Titled "Great Bridge Builders: Edgar Snow and International Friends in Yan'an", the exhibition features 150 cultural relics and archival documents, 402 photographs, and seven documentaries. It tells the stories of international friends who broke through multiple blockades to reach Yan'an, China's revolutionary heartland, about 90 years ago, supported the Chinese revolution, and helped build a bridge of dialogue between the CPC, the Chinese people, and the world. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March by the Red Army under the leadership of the CPC, and also the 90th anniversary of Snow's first visit to the revolutionary base in northern Shaanxi, which inspired his renowned work "Red Star Over China." His works helped introduce the Chinese revolution in the 1930s to the world and inspired many other international people to visit Yan'an. The exhibition is co-hosted by the publicity department of the CPC Shaanxi provincial committee, the Museum of the CPC and the CPC Yan'an municipal committee, and organized by the Yan'an Revolutionary Memorial Hall. Highlights include a 1938 Chinese edition of Red Star Over China published in Shanghai, and an inscribed copy of Helen Snow's Inside Red China. Liu Ni, director of the Yan'an Revolutionary Memorial Hall, said that more items are being donated. For instance, Sharon Crain, a friend of Edgar Snow's wife Helen, donated two suitcases the couple once used. The suitcases are currently on the way to China. Visitors can also find items such as a camera used by American doctor George Hatem in Yan'an, a replica of German doctor Hans Muller's wallet, and documents from American experts Erwin Engst and Joan Hinton. "As descendants visiting this exhibition, viewing these artifacts and archival photos, we gain a deeper appreciation for the simple yet profound friendship our ancestors forged when they chose to put down roots in this land," said Dehua Muller, son of Hans. "We are committed to passing this friendship on." Fred Engst, son of Erwin Engst and Joan Hinton, observed that while official diplomacy serves as a "big bridge" between nations, people-to-people exchanges form the "small bridges." He explained: "The big bridge bears the critical mission of connecting countries, while the smaller bridges link the hearts of ordinary people. Only when both converge can mutual understanding truly endure." The exhibition will last for three months in Beijing. ■ A man visits an exhibition at the Museum of the Communist Party of China in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 23, 2026. item.title: Decoding Shenzhen: the city that wowed APEC leaders
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
* The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting has just wrapped up in China's Shenzhen, and the leaders did not leave the host city without a comment. On various occasions, they praised the city's futuristic vibe and meteoric rise. * Shenzhen is often seen as the epitome of China's development over more than four decades. It has risen from a small fishing village to the window of China's reform and opening up, and then to an innovation hub and home to tech giants such as Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI. * In 2025, Shenzhen's GDP soared to 3.87 trillion yuan (about 576.58 billion U.S. dollars), 14,000 times its GDP in 1980, a pace rare in the history of global urbanization. The same year, Shenzhen's total R&D investment reached 245.31 billion yuan, or 6.67 percent of its GDP, with enterprises accounting for more than 93 percent of total R&D investment. * Shenzhen's trade with other APEC economies has grown more than tenfold in nearly three decades, surging from 267.5 billion yuan in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan in 2025. Multinational companies are placing not only R&D centers and regional headquarters in Shenzhen, but also their long-term strategic commitments. SHENZHEN, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting has just wrapped up in China's Shenzhen, and the leaders did not leave the host city without a comment. On various occasions, they praised the city's futuristic vibe and meteoric rise. During his stay in Shenzhen, Russian President Vladimir Putin called the southern Chinese city in Guangdong Province "impressive," hailing it as one of the world's most advanced and dynamic metropolises. He noted that the city organically combines a high level of urbanization, a comfortable urban environment and an innovative production base. As one of the key investment centers in the Asia-Pacific, Shenzhen reflects the profound technological, economic and social transformations taking place in China and across Asia, Putin said. U.S. President Donald Trump, back in Washington after his APEC trip, spoke highly of Shenzhen at a White House press conference. "When you were there, you could see it. It was amazing energy," he said, adding that the city is clean and immaculate, and it has been built in a short period of time. Recalling his first visit to Shenzhen in 1998, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the city as an example of the Asia-Pacific region's extraordinary rise. "If you had put two photos together, 1998 and 2026, you would not think it was the same place," the prime minister said. China's achievement "is worth celebrating and should certainly not be taken for granted," he added. Shenzhen is often seen as the epitome of China's development over more than four decades. It has risen from a small fishing village to the window of China's reform and opening up, and then to an innovation hub and home to tech giants such as Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI. Even before hosting the APEC event, Shenzhen had already become one of China's top spots for international tourists, while drawing global media spotlight for its rapid growth and technological prowess. ENGINE OF INNOVATION When Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, was designated a special economic zone in 1980, it was a border town of just over 300,000 people, its roads narrow and its industrial base virtually nonexistent. Today, it is a megacity of more than 18 million residents, its skyline dense with high-rises and its streets thick with traffic. In 2025, Shenzhen's GDP soared to 3.87 trillion yuan (about 576.58 billion U.S. dollars), 14,000 times its GDP in 1980, a pace rare in the history of global urbanization. "Shenzhen's success offers many lessons. In many ways, it is China's own success story in miniature," said Ameen Muneer Mohammed Al-Obaidi, a reporter with China Arab TV. More recently, the city has evolved from a world factory into an innovation and advanced manufacturing hub with vibrant industry clusters spanning sectors from new energy to artificial intelligence (AI). Drones zip across city blocks, streets buzz with electric vehicles, and an AI industry booms -- this is the Shenzhen that President of the Republic of Korea Lee Jae Myung saw during the APEC meeting. The city serves as a vivid testament to how future technologies can transform our lives, and technologies once considered part of the distant future have already become part of daily life here, Lee said. Experts have accredited Shenzhen's leading position in multiple technological fronts to the city's heavy investment in research and development (R&D). Data shows that in 2025, Shenzhen's total R&D investment reached 245.31 billion yuan, or 6.67 percent of its GDP, with enterprises accounting for more than 93 percent of total R&D investment. The city also draws strength from the manufacturing prowess in the Pearl River Delta and integrated growth in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a major cross-sea transportation project that opened to traffic in 2024, has prompted Shenzhen companies to set up factories in cities like Zhongshan to benefit from their manufacturing capacity and larger industrial space. At Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen's mega electronics marketplace, a design can be sketched in the morning, turned into a prototype by afternoon, mass-produced the next day, and shipped overseas within a week. About 3 million parcels leave the area every day. Huaqiangbei welcomed nearly 8,000 foreign buyers on an average day this year, according to local government. Janwick Hattingh, from South Africa, bought a power bank there. "It's quite advanced here," he said. "You can find any tech product you can think of." MODEL OF COOPERATION Addressing the APEC CEO Summit, held on Nov. 17-18 on the sidelines of the APEC meeting, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul named Shenzhen the best-fitting place for Asia-Pacific economies to discuss how to adapt to a changing world and build a more prosperous future together. The city, he said, shows what transformation can achieve when an economy opens itself to the world. Openness is in Shenzhen's DNA. For more than four decades, Shenzhen has kept opening wider to the world. In the first 10 months of this year, its imports and exports reached 5.25 trillion yuan, up 40.9 percent year on year. During the Shenzhen meeting, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and his wife visited a local fruit shop to celebrate the arrival in China of new-season Chilean cherries and invited Chinese consumers to taste them. The timing was no accident. China is currently the largest export destination for Chilean cherries. Kast noted that Chile will expand the scale of trade and investment cooperation with China, broaden collaboration in agriculture, mining, new energy vehicles, infrastructure development and AI, and promote exchanges in education and culture. Cherries are just one part of a much larger flow in Asia-Pacific cooperation. Shenzhen's trade with other APEC economies has grown more than tenfold in nearly three decades, surging from 267.5 billion yuan in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan in 2025. Multinational companies are placing not only R&D centers and regional headquarters in Shenzhen, but also their long-term strategic commitments. Apple has set up an applied research lab in the city, while DHL Express has put its Shenzhen super gateway into operation, its largest single investment project in the Chinese mainland to date. Cooperation between Shenzhen and other APEC economies is shifting from "bringing in" to "creating together." Teo Siong Seng, executive chairman of Pacific International Lines in Singapore, noted that six of the world's ten largest container ports, including Shenzhen, are in China. He expressed hope that APEC will further expand regional connectivity and make the connections among its members more resilient and sustainable. "As the Chinese proverb reminds us, 'hai na bai chuan,' which means the sea is vast because it embraces the waters of many rivers," said Kristalina Georgieva, managing director of the International Monetary Fund. "When we pull together, what comes into view is shared prosperity and peace." (Reporting by Cui Enhui, Wang Jian, Yao Yuan, Wang Pan and Sun Fei; Video reporters: Huo Siying and Wang Ruiping; Video editors: Zheng Xin, Mu Xuyao, Zheng Qingbin, Hong Liang and Hong Yan) ■

item.title: China, EU hold 17th economic, financial dialogue in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
BEIJING, Nov. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 17th China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue was held in Beijing on Monday, with both sides discussing macroeconomic conditions and policies, as well as China-EU multilateral cooperation within the G20. China's Vice Minister of Finance Liao Min, who co-chaired the dialogue, said that under the current circumstances, China and the EU should jointly uphold and practice true multilateralism and work toward an open world economy to inject greater stability and certainty into the global economy. Major economies, including China and the EU, should take necessary measures to advance structural reforms, deepen macroeconomic policy coordination, keep global industrial and supply chains stable and smooth, and promote global economic and financial stability, Liao said. China is ready to expand mutual openness with the EU and make the cooperation pie bigger, Liao added, calling on the EU side to respect market economy principles and fair competition, and provide a fair, just and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises. Noting that the China-EU Economic and Financial Dialogue is an important platform for the two sides to deepen macroeconomic policy coordination and strengthen financial and economic cooperation, the EU side said it values macroeconomic policy communication and practical cooperation with China. The EU side said it is willing to strengthen constructive dialogue with China on the basis of mutual respect and reciprocal openness, carry out equal and mutually beneficial cooperation, properly address differences and disagreements, and advance the rebalancing of EU-China economic relations in an orderly manner. ■
